sections.heading: Overview
bullets: Daniel Ortiz and Priya Raman met Elena Voss and Tom Brandt to evaluate Kestrel Dispatch for Acme Freight's 140-truck regional fleet.
The group designed a conditional two-week pilot on Acme's north corridor and named data mapping and security approval as gates before live use.

sections.heading: Key points
bullets: Tom said seven dispatchers use a shared load sheet plus personal copies, with driver updates passed by phone and reconciled across shifts.
Elena said customers lack live ETAs, two late deliveries last Tuesday were reported by receivers first, and a large account escalated three missed windows last month.
Tom estimated about 30 customer status calls on a busy Monday and said idle trucks occur when dispatchers miss a ready next load.
The proposed pilot covers about 20 trucks, two dispatchers, one north-corridor lane, and one customer contact after security approval.
Elena has roughly $60,000 in approved annual software budget and must choose among Kestrel Dispatch and two competitors by the end of next month.

sections.heading: Decisions
bullets: Elena and Tom accepted an active-record-only pilot that would import drivers, vehicles, and open loads, without moving six years of history.
The two-week measurement period will begin only after Tom approves the field mapping and Acme's security team clears live pilot access.
The scorecard will cover earlier warning of late arrivals, status calls, dispatcher use, missing inputs, and import exceptions rather than promise fewer late deliveries.

sections.heading: Open questions
bullets: Tom still needs to confirm that inconsistent customer codes can be mapped safely from a scrubbed 50-row sample and that dispatchers can correct wrong records.
Acme's security lead must decide whether the packet permits live pilot access and a customer-facing status view.
Acme has not selected a vendor or approved a purchase, pending pilot evidence, operations review, and security approval.

sections.heading: Pain points
bullets: Tom said Acme's seven dispatchers reconcile separate spreadsheet copies and phone updates for a 140-truck fleet.
Elena said late deliveries can surface through receivers before Acme's team knows about them, while customers have no live ETA view.
Tom estimated about 30 customer status calls on a busy Monday and described idle drivers caused by delayed assignment visibility.

sections.heading: Current solution
bullets: Acme dispatches with a shared load spreadsheet, personal dispatcher copies, driver phone calls, and manual appointment times.
Tom said old driver IDs and inconsistent customer codes make the workbook unsuitable for an unchecked full import.

sections.heading: Budget and timeline
bullets: Elena said roughly $60,000 per year of software budget is approved, while any setup cost needs separate review.
Elena must select among Kestrel Dispatch and two competitors by the end of next month, after operations and security reviews.
Daniel said the two-week pilot clock will start after mapping and security approval, so preparation does not reduce live measurement time.

sections.heading: Objections
bullets: Tom objected that a dashboard-only pilot or months of double entry would not prove that dispatchers can run a real shift.
Tom worried that six years of inconsistent spreadsheet history and customer codes would make migration painful or link loads to the wrong customers.
Elena said Acme requires a security review before production access or any real customer-facing pilot status.

sections.heading: Next steps
bullets: Daniel will send a security packet tomorrow and a scoped pilot proposal with annual pricing by end of week.
Tom will send a scrubbed 50-row export by Friday, including awkward customer codes, and Priya will review its field mapping with him.
Elena will introduce Acme's security lead next week, and Priya will draft the pilot scorecard and rollback outline.

sections.heading: Today
bullets: Daniel Ortiz will prepare the security packet for tomorrow and the scoped pilot and pricing proposal for end of week.
Priya Raman will draft a north-corridor scorecard and rollback outline for a two-week pilot covering about 20 trucks and two dispatchers.
Tom Brandt will prepare a scrubbed 50-row sample with difficult customer codes for review by Friday.
Elena Voss will introduce Acme's security lead next week so the team can assess pilot access and customer status visibility.

sections.heading: Blockers
bullets: Tom Brandt needs to see that unmatched customer codes are flagged and wrong imported records can be corrected without moving six years of history.
Elena Voss requires security approval before Acme grants production access or exposes real customer-facing pilot statuses.

sections.heading: Goals
bullets: Elena wants credible live ETAs and evidence that dispatchers will use Kestrel Dispatch before choosing software for Acme's 140-truck fleet.
Priya proposed measuring earlier warning, status calls, dispatcher use, and import exceptions during two weeks of live north-corridor use.

sections.heading: Progress
bullets: Elena and Tom agreed in principle to a pilot of about 20 trucks, two dispatchers, and one customer contact after security approval.
Tom said an active-only import and a 50-row mapping review reduced his concern about moving six years of spreadsheet history.

sections.heading: Risks
bullets: Tom warned that inconsistent customer codes can link loads to the wrong account and that a pilot requiring double entry would fail on the dispatch floor.
Elena said Acme's security review is mandatory before live access or a customer-facing status view.
Priya cautioned that a two-week pilot cannot promise fewer late deliveries because dock delays and traffic still affect actual arrival times.

sections.heading: Decisions
bullets: The pilot will use active drivers, vehicles, and open loads on the north corridor, with unmatched customer codes stopped for review.
Tom's mapping sign-off and Acme's security clearance are gates before the two-week live-use period begins.
Elena will compare Kestrel Dispatch with two competitors using operational adoption and ETA evidence rather than a dashboard demonstration alone.

sections.heading: Next steps
bullets: Tom will export 50 scrubbed rows by Friday, and Priya will return a mapping and exception list for review.
Daniel will send a security packet tomorrow and a scoped proposal with annual pricing by end of week.
Elena will introduce Acme's security lead next week, while Priya prepares the scorecard and rollback outline.
